newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Heavier rains water Ivory Coast's cocoa belt.
newsitem.headline: Heavier rains water Ivory Coast's cocoa belt.

text.p: Ivory Coast's mid-crop cocoa prospects may be boosted by heavier rains recorded in early December, but bean drying difficulties will continue, weather and crop analysts said.

"Mid-crop prospects will be clearer about two to three weeks after the rains," said a crop analyst. "If we had another 20-40mm by the end of this month we would probably be heading for an average mid-crop, but predictions now are impossible."
Data show average rains up by over 25 percent from the end of November, with 45mm falling at each of nine monitoring stations in the 10 days to December 10.
About 30mm fell in the last third of November.
"Rains are strongest in the south but falling throughout the country as the Harmattan (dry conditions) has still not moved south," said the weather analyst.
One local analyst back from a tour of plantations to assess mid-crop developments said rains had fallen in most cocoa areas on four out of seven days.
Weather data show over half the 400mm total was recorded in coastal and southwestern areas around Tabou and San Pedro.

Northern and central areas around Man, Dimbokro and Yamassoukro also had rains as a weather front associated with dry conditions retreated to Ivory Coast's northern borders. Rains remained constant around Gagnoa in the centre-west.
"When the rains stop, flowers will develop and insect activity will get under way," said the crop analyst.
Another crop analyst said extended December showers last year had been followed by a bumper mid-crop.
Overall weather patterns have puzzled observers.
Heavy downpours in July and August were twice the long-term average and a short rainy season in September and October turned out to be dry with rains only falling from November.
Up-country buyers say some bush tracks have deteriorated and cocoa drying difficulties have continued. Bean humidity levels recorded at ports stand at about 8-10 percent.
The data, from Ivory Coast's national weather station, showed rainfall for the first 10 days of December for the following key growing areas plus the commercial capital Abidjan were -
Dalao 1.1 mm, Gagnoa 17.4 mm, Abidjan 42.5 mm, San Pedro 97.6 mm, Tabou 152.5mm and Man 25.9 mm.
